events.credibility_reason: Content never read; conflicting bibliographic records. Nothing establishes what it proves.

Mailing-list claim of a full proof of a famous open problem; a participant reported a false step; no reply, no revision, no uptake in 24 years; every later source (Wikipedia, Klaška 2026, Open Problem Garden) still calls the problem open. The reported critique is garbled as summarised, so not knocked_down, but the claim is set aside.

Anonymous page; every progress claim labelled source-reported and unaudited; certificate not executed; inconsistent dates; no uptake. Its band exclusions restrict carry configurations, not a class of n, and its n<=10 completion is finite instances from published factorisations.
Self-published v0.1 with no review; Lean status is the author's own claim; and it concerns multiplicative orders, not square factors.

why: No event settles, restricts or bounds the question 'are all Fermat numbers square-free?'. Warren-Bray 1967 is a reduction to the Wieferich condition (none). Björn-Riesel is a heuristic (none). New prime factors of composite F_n, Klaška's Mersenne and mod-p papers, the Erdős #1209 variants and Fujimoto's order computations are different questions (variant). Klaška 2026, as far as anything readable shows, restates the hypothesis as open (none). The close call was ProofAtlas. Its band exclusions are not restrictions to a class of n. Its finite completion to n<=10 is instances already known from factorisations, and the page disclaims any proof, so it is none and doubtful. Basaldúa's 2001 claim is set aside as not credible: it is an old mailing-list proof of a famous problem, it drew an unanswered critique, it was taken up by no one, and later literature still calls the problem open. The AI credits do not count. Fujimoto's 'Co-architect' label says nothing about what Claude or Rei produced, and in any case the paper is off-question. The Erdős thread has no systems entry. Both are none.
doubts: Klaška's Integers A77 full text was never read. If it contains a partial result (a class of n proved square-free), that event would become a case. Its AI acknowledgements are also unread. Its 'digested' rests on journal acceptance reported in a search excerpt.
